imageAlt: Golfer standing with their ball in bounds near an out of bounds line, reaching to remove a chair just out of bounds that interferes with their stance.

sceneSpec.setting: The edge of a golf hole marked with white out of bounds stakes, with both in bounds and out of bounds areas visible.
sceneSpec.players: One player preparing to play a stroke near the edge of the course. The player is reaching towards a movable obstruction just beyond the out of bounds line.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: The ball is clearly in bounds, near but not touching the out of bounds line.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The moment Jezz is removing the movable obstruction from out of bounds, before taking his stance.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Highlighting that a player may remove a movable obstruction interfering with their stance, even if it lies out of bounds.
mustShow: Player’s ball in bounds close to the out of bounds line
Movable obstruction (such as a chair or similar item) positioned out of bounds but within reach, interfering with the player's stance
Player in the act of removing the obstruction

questions.title: Moving Something in the Way Even If It's Out of Bounds
questions.question: Jezz's ball is on the golf course, but something he can move, like a can, is just outside the course and gets in the way of where he stands. Jezz moves it out of the way. What happens now?

choices.text: Jezz gets one extra shot as a penalty.
Jezz does not get any penalty.

questions.explanation: You can move things like cans or bottles out of your way, even if they are off the course. You don't get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Something on or near the golf course like a can or bottle, that you can pick up and move.
A place outside the golf course where you are not supposed to play.

questions.teachingTip: Let children practise spotting things they can and cannot move, like twigs or bins, and teach why out of bounds things can be moved, too.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they can't move things that are out of bounds, even if those things are in their way.
Children may worry about getting a penalty for moving things that are off the course.

questions.title: Movable obstruction interfering with stance but out of bounds
questions.question: Jezz’s ball is in bounds, but a movable obstruction that is out of bounds interferes with his stance. He removes the movable obstruction. What is the ruling?
questions.explanation: Under Rule 15.2a, a player may remove a movable obstruction anywhere on or off the course without penalty.
